task: Compare caching approaches for this workload and recommend a decision or next experiment. Use the supplied quantities; do not invent measurements.
context: A process has 512 MiB total memory, with 320 MiB already needed for other work. Expected distinct keys: 5,000,000; retained bytes per key including overhead: 200. Added request latency must stay below 10 ms. Options under discussion: retain all keys locally; use a bounded 128 MiB local cache; use a shared cache whose measured added round-trip latency is 2 ms in the target region. Local bounded-cache hit rate and shared-cache outage behavior have not been measured. Source reads take 15 ms when uncached.
expected: Calculates that retaining all keys needs about 1,000,000,000 bytes and violates the available memory constraint.
Compares bounded local and shared approaches fairly, identifying the unknown hit rate and outage behavior.
Avoids an unconditional latency guarantee; identifies a discriminating workload replay or outage observation.
forbidden: Selecting an unbounded local cache as feasible under the stated memory limit.
Inventing a hit ratio or using an unexplained score to hide the missing evidence.
evidence: Feasibility arithmetic, comparison table or prose, stated unknowns and recommendation conditions.
